questions.explain: The chapter argues the advantage is domain specificity: a custom model learns the unique patterns of your environment (Monday-morning OLTP clusters, 2 AM ETL quirks, connection-pool lock behavior) that no public training set can capture.
options: Custom models learn the unique patterns of your own telemetry — your workload's seasonality, ETL quirks, and connection-pool behavior — which no generic public model can capture
Custom models are cheaper to train than prompting a generic LLM
A generic LLM cannot access SQL Server DMVs
Custom models never drift, while generic LLMs drift with every workload change
questions.q: Why do custom ML models built on your own telemetry outperform generic AI for quantitative database operations problems?

questions.explain: The chapter emphasizes wrapping hour-of-day as sin/cos components so the model understands that hour 23 and hour 0 are adjacent rather than opposite ends of the scale — meaningfully improving anomaly detection for workloads with daily patterns.
options: It doubles the number of temporal features to give the model more capacity
It removes seasonality entirely so anomalies stand out more clearly
It converts 24-hour clock values into the local timezone of the monitored instance
Hour 23 and hour 0 become adjacent on the encoded circle instead of opposite ends of a linear scale, which improves accuracy for workloads with strong daily patterns
questions.q: What is the purpose of the cyclical time encoding (hour_sin/hour_cos) in the feature engineering pipeline?

questions.explain: Isolation Forest randomly partitions the feature space and needs no labeled data — it requires no tagged past incidents — with contamination=0.03 expressing the prior belief that ~3% of samples are anomalous, and the threshold set at the 3rd percentile of training scores.
options: It requires a large labeled dataset of tagged past incidents to learn the anomaly class boundary
It is unsupervised — no labeled data required — and contamination=0.03 means the model expects roughly 3% of samples to be anomalous
It fits a linear trend to each metric and flags deviations larger than three standard deviations
It requires at least 90 days of incident-labeled data before the first training run
questions.q: Why is Isolation Forest the chapter's first choice for DBA anomaly detection, and what does contamination=0.03 mean?

questions.explain: The chapter sets changepoint_prior_scale=0.05 deliberately conservatively so the forecast recognizes genuine trend changes without overfitting to normal variance like daily backups and index maintenance.
options: 0.05 is Prophet's default and should never be changed
It makes the model react faster to sudden capacity spikes, triggering alerts sooner
It is deliberately conservative so the model recognizes genuine trend changes without overfitting to normal variance such as daily backup and index maintenance activity
It disables changepoint detection so the forecast stays linear regardless of workload shifts
questions.q: In the Prophet capacity-forecasting model, why is changepoint_prior_scale set to the conservative value of 0.05?

questions.explain: TimeSeriesSplit is non-negotiable because standard random cross-validation leaks future information into training folds and produces optimistic accuracy estimates; the label is also shifted backward by the lookahead window so the model predicts storms N minutes in advance.
options: TimeSeriesSplit ensures validation always uses earlier data than training, because random cross-validation leaks future data into training folds and gives optimistic accuracy estimates; the target label is shifted backward by the lookahead window (e.g., 5 minutes)
Gradient boosting requires the features to be scaled first, which TimeSeriesSplit performs automatically
TimeSeriesSplit is faster than random CV on the 15-second-interval snapshot data
Random cross-validation is fine as long as you set random_state=42, so TimeSeriesSplit is optional
questions.q: For the lock storm predictor, why is TimeSeriesSplit cross-validation mandatory, and how is the target label handled?
